text.p: Solidere began a long-awaited rise on the Beirut Stock Exchange in the week ended on Friday and brokers said they expected the shares to rise further next week.
"Next week should be Solidere's week," broker Carole Deeb of Credit Commercial et Foncier told Reuters.

Bank shares also rose, but Bank of Beirut appeared to lose steam after surging 67 percent in less than three weeks after its April 11 listing and fell back slightly on Wednesday from $3.625 to $3.5625.
Brokers said they expected bank shares to stabilise in a firm market next week while investors turned to Solidere.
"Bank shares are expected to remain stable next week," Deeb said.

Solidere A and B shares both rose for the first time in weeks, reaching $11 from $10.25 and $10.75 respectively and dealers said a surge by the company's Global Depositary Receipts in London stimulated the rise.

The GDRs, issued last November at $11.5, soared on the London Stock Exchange on Tuesday to $17.625 from last week's $12 and the company said purchases by U.S. and European emerging market funds were behind the increase. The GDRs traded at $16 on Friday.
An expected approval of a 25 cents dividend on the shares at a general assembly scheduled for May 27 should push prices further up, dealers said.
"The expected announcement of a dividend should increase demand on the shares throughout the month," Deeb said.
Among the bank shares, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose 5.6 percent to $16.625 from $15.75 last Thursday while Banque Audi rose 0.6 percent to $20.125 from $20.
BLC and Audi have risen 47.7 and 34.1 percent respectively since their December and January debuts.
Total demand for bank shares fell to 943,832 shares from last week's 3,722,755. The major drop was in demand for BOB which fell to 594,378 from 3,322,161 shares.
Demand for BLC fell to 160,397 shares from 204,715 while demand for Audi fell slightly to 189,060 from 195,879.
Supply for bank shares also fell sharply to 601,237 from 2,169,280 shares last week.

"Investors are more or less satisfied with the levels shares have reached. I expect a firm market next week with no excessive demand or supply but a normal flow that reflects investors' needs," Deeb said.
The LIBX bank index rose 2.63 percent on the week to 138.04. The BLOM general index rose 4.35 percent to 953.96 while the LISPI fell 0.19 percent to 87.01.

Total BSE turnover for the week, shortened to three days by public holidays was 938,421 shares for a value of $8,133,821 against 2,487,970 shares for a value of $15,263,089 during four working days last week.

Of the four listed industrial firms pipemaker Eternit fell to $1.8125 from $2, Ciments Libanais was unchanged at $1.28125. Ciments Blancs, trading for the first time since April 15, fell to $5 from $5.5.
There was no trade in tilemaker Uniceramic.
- Zeina Soufan, Beirut editorial (9611) 602057 745307
